sanskrit_verse: चलं निरस्य भूतेन व्यवहारान् नयेन् नृपः / भूतम् अप्य् अनुपन्यस्तं हीयते व्यवहारतः //
transliteration: chalaṃ nirasya bhūtena vyavahārān nayen nṛpaḥ / bhūtam apy anupanyastaṃ hīyate vyavahārataḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: The king shall conduct transactions by dismissing the transient; even what is existent, if unplaced in dharma, is diminished through transactional engagement.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in alignment with immutable dharma, not mutable phenomena
Causation arises from dharmic placement, not material presence
Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment between the real and the changeful
Restoration logic demands withdrawal from that which distorts truth-value
Consciousness alignment necessitates governance beyond sensory transaction
executable_legal_axioms: IF a legal act involves chala (deception or instability), THEN it MUST be excluded from judicial consideration
IF an entity exists BUT lacks dharmic foundation, THEN its legal weight SHALL be nullified
IF a ruler engages in vyavahara without rejecting the transient, THEN the transaction SHALL be deemed invalid
IF a case includes elements ungrounded in satya-dharma, THEN automated dismissal SHALL occur
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, any litigation founded upon unstable or deceptive premises must be dismissed ex officio. The threshold of responsibility lies in recognizing the distinction between apparent existence and dharmic validity. Authority derives not from factual assertion alone, but from alignment with the eternal law.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that only that which is placed in dharma bears legal consequence. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that neglect of foundational truth leads to diminishment in outcome. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of alignment to sanatana dharma. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that misalignment naturally results in ineffectiveness, not imposed penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate pratyākhyāna process to withdraw consent from all unstable agreements
Engage dhāraṇā protocol to stabilize consciousness of parties involved
Implement sattva-restoration for rulers who have engaged in transient-based transactions
Realign vyavahāra frameworks with akṣara-dharma through śuddhi-kriyā
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this verse executes as pure Dharma. Justice flows not through punishment, but through the conscious rejection of the unreal. The transient is dismissed; the Real abides. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
